question: What is the main purpose of an Automated External Defibrillator?

options.A: To restore a normal heart rhythm
options.C: To pump blood for the patient

explanation: The device analyzes heart rhythms and delivers a shock if needed to reset chaotic electrical activity. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h1)

question: Why is early defibrillation so vital for a person in cardiac arrest?

options.A: Survival chances drop with every passing minute
options.B: It cures the underlying cause of the heart attack
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.D: It prevents the lungs from filling with fluid

explanation: Quick delivery of an electrical shock drastically improves the odds of a successful resuscitation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h1)

question: Which heart rhythm is classified as shockable by an AED?
explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a chaotic, quivering rhythm that requires an immediate electric shock. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h2)

question: What action does the AED take when it detects asystole in a patient?

options.B: Sounds a continuous alarm until reset
options.C: Waits for a physician to approve a shock
options.D: Instructs the rescuer to continue CPR

explanation: Asystole is a flatline rhythm where shocks are ineffective, so the device tells rescuers to resume compressions. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h2)

question: What item is typically found inside the AED preparation kit?

options.B: A razor to remove chest hair

explanation: A razor is included to ensure good pad adhesion by removing excessive chest hair. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h3)

question: Why does an AED unit perform routine self-tests?

options.A: To confirm the battery and system are operational
options.B: To drain old power before charging fresh cells
options.C: To automatically update the software version
options.D: To calibrate the internal clock for local time

explanation: Self-tests ensure the device will function properly when an emergency occurs. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h3)

question: What is the very first step when operating an AED during an emergency?
explanation: Powering on the device activates the voice prompts that guide the rest of the rescue process. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing to deliver a shock with an AED. What action must happen immediately before pressing the shock button?

options.A: Ventilate the lungs with a bag-valve-mask
options.B: Ensure no one is touching the patient
options.D: Check the patient's pupils for reactivity

explanation: Rescuers must clear the patient so nobody else receives the accidental discharge of electrical energy. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h4)

question: How do chest compressions assist the AED process?

options.A: They generate enough electrical current to reset the heart
options.B: They replace the need for adhesive electrode pads
options.C: They make the heart muscle more responsive to the shock

explanation: Circulating blood delivers oxygen to the myocardium, increasing the likelihood that defibrillation will succeed. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h5)

question: When should chest compressions resume after an AED delivers a shock?
explanation: Rescuers should go right back to chest compressions without pausing to check for a pulse right after a shock. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h5)

question: What adjustment is necessary if a patient has an implanted pacemaker visible on the upper chest?

options.A: Cancel the shock and rely solely on medications
options.B: Place the AED pad at least one inch away from it
options.C: Turn off the pacemaker using a magnet before use
options.D: Increase the energy setting on the device

explanation: Placing pads directly over a device can block the shock energy and damage the implanted hardware. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h6)

question: Which group requires the use of pediatric attenuation pads or settings?
explanation: Pediatric pads reduce the energy level delivered to match the smaller body size of young children. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary indicator that an AED is ready for use during a routine check?
explanation: A flashing status indicator shows that the device passed its internal diagnostic self-test. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h7)

question: Why must a nurse check the expiration dates on AED pads regularly?

options.A: The conductive gel on the pads can dry out over time
options.B: Expired pads will drain the internal battery quickly
options.C: The plastic housing becomes brittle and cracks
options.D: The device will refuse to turn on if supplies are old

explanation: Dry gel fails to transmit the electrical shock effectively to the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h7)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility immediately after a patient is successfully resuscitated with an AED?

options.A: Discharge the patient to the general ward
options.B: Remove the electrode pads from the patient's chest
options.C: Monitor vital signs and maintain airway patency
options.D: Immediately clean and store the AED unit away

explanation: Post-resuscitation care focuses on stabilizing the patient and preventing secondary injury. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h8)

question: What information should be included in the nursing documentation following an AED event?

options.A: The names of all visitors in the room
options.B: The cost of the replacement electrode pads
options.C: The brand name of the hospital bed

explanation: Recording interventions like the number of shocks provides a complete medical record for the care team. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h8)
